notes.claim: In a resistor, voltage and current are in phase: both curves reach maxima and minima together.
The product of rms voltage and rms current in a resistor equals the average power.
The instantaneous power in a resistor oscillates at twice the frequency of the voltage and never goes negative.

sources.title: 2.8 Power and energy in resistive circuits – Applied Electrical Engineering Fundamentals
sources.quote: Note that the product of the RMS voltage and RMS current is equal to the average power:

sources.title: Lessons In Electric Circuits -- Volume II (AC) - Chapter 11
sources.quote: Also note that the waveform for power is not at the same frequency as the voltage or current! Rather, its frequency is double that of either the voltage or current waveforms.

sources.title: 15.2 Simple AC Circuits - University Physics Volume 2 | OpenStax
sources.quote: Both curves reach their maxima and minima at the same times, that is, the current through and the voltage across the resistor are in phase.

sources.title: Lessons In Electric Circuits -- Volume II (AC) - Chapter 11
sources.quote: Note that the waveform for power is always positive, never negative for this resistive circuit. This means that power is always being dissipated by the resistive load, and never returned to the source as it is with reactive loads.
